clue.text: Eccentric afraid heir is light-headed?

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd and out of the ordinary, so the following letters are set in an odd new order

blocks.note: the two words supply all ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball heir, frightened and dizzy, feels faint.
explanation.walkthrough: Light-headed normally means dizzy; the question mark lets it mean having pale, blond hair instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, a person whose head looks light has blond or pale hair, a whimsical cryptic reading.

clue.text: Defence of boxer protecting middle of ribs

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one piece wraps around the other
asks for only the central letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer
the central two letters of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: A boxer guards his midriff, shielding his ribs from punches.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is the claim of being elsewhere, offered in court as a defence against an accusation.

clue.text: Damaged trailer is the result of faulty hearing?

indicators.note: something damaged is broken out of shape, so the word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wrecked trailer is blamed on someone mishearing instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Faulty hearing suggests deafness, but the hearing is a court case: a flawed trial is often run again.
explanation.definitionFit: When a court case is conducted improperly, a judge may order the case tried again before a new jury.

clue.text: Song from musical in East London

indicators.note: Cockney speakers of East London famously drop the H sound at the start of words

blocks.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: A number taken from a show staged in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken by a Cockney, Hair loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, a standard word for a simple song.

clue.text: Outlaw to steal from home with US gangster

blocks.note: to rob is to steal
at home means in
hood is American slang for a hoodlum

explanation.surface: A criminal plans a burglary alongside an American mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend of stealing from the rich echoes in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary English hero of Sherwood Forest was declared an outlaw for robbing the rich.

clue.text: Number like one thousand, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
the Roman numeral for one
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A large figure such as a thousand, mainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a comparison, but it is a verb meaning enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any single numeral from zero to nine, so it is a kind of figure.

clue.text: Pulse is fast on crossword setter over fifty

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
the setter refers to himself as I
the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler past fifty fasts and checks his heart rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulse looks like a heartbeat but is the edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the dried edible seeds of legumes, and a lentil is one such seed.

clue.text: You shouldn’t drop this group of baby mammals

blocks.note: first meaning: rubbish discarded in a public place
second meaning: the young born to an animal at one time

explanation.surface: A warning not to drop a newborn cub or puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both discarded rubbish in the street and the young produced in one birth by a cat, dog or pig.

clue.text: London attraction — a challenge for Scottish hillwalker?

blocks.note: first meaning: the great bell and clock tower at Westminster
second meaning: in Scotland a ben is a mountain, and a large one is a challenge

explanation.surface: Comparing a London sight with a tough Highland climb.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben is the Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Westminster bell draws tourists, and read literally a large Scottish peak tests any walker.

clue.text: Big road filled by trendy car

indicators.note: something filled by another holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written with I for 1
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A motorway full of fashionable small cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is the classic small British car model first made in 1959.

clue.text: Add explanations to article on revolutionary gallery

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: the indefinite article
taken as written before being turned
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Adding captions to a piece about a radical art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to write notes or comments on it, clarifying its meaning.

clue.text: Promote and devise art in a novel way

indicators.note: doing something in a novel way means doing it differently, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Marketing advice: push your product and design creative visuals.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise a product is to publicise it to the public so that more people buy it.

clue.text: One who induced drooling with unfinished dessert

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a pavlova is a meringue dessert topped with cream and fruit

explanation.surface: Someone made people's mouths water with a half-eaten pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The dessert was named after a ballerina, but the trimmed word is the Russian scientist famous for conditioning dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov trained dogs to salivate at a bell signal in his classic conditioning experiments.

clue.text: Beast in area north of Milan, camouflaged

indicators.note: camouflage disguises a thing's appearance, so the letters are rearranged to hide them

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disguised creature lurks somewhere north of an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, north of means placed above, so the single letter comes before the city before the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature, particularly a large wild one, as opposed to a human or plant.

clue.text: Orator gutted by friend using speech

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outside letters of the word

blocks.note: the first and last letters
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A speaker is devastated when a companion steals his speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something orally means doing it by mouth, in spoken rather than written form.

clue.text: Everybody, say, runs round pretty quickly

blocks.note: all means everybody
e.g. means for example
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Everyone, for instance, jogs round the track rather fast.
explanation.walkthrough: In music, the term marks a brisk tempo, a little slower than presto.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the Italian musical direction for a lively, fairly fast tempo, so it means rather briskly.

clue.text: Nicked criminal freed after leaders of police ignored laws

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letters of the words are kept
criminal suggests something crooked and bent out of line, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letters of the three words
the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook was arrested and then released after police chiefs ignored the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicked looks like arrested, matching the police surface, but here it means stolen; nicked is British slang for both.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilfer is to steal small items, and nicked is British slang for stolen.

clue.text: Spanish ruler’s cut old bread in Geneva

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter of the name is dropped

blocks.note: General Franco ruled Spain from 1939 to 1975

explanation.surface: A Spanish dictator slices a stale loaf in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money; the clue is fair for Geneva, where the currency is still used.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for cash, and the franc is the currency of Switzerland and formerly France.

clue.text: Go red in the face after bishop leaves drunk

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: to blush is to go red with embarrassment
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone flushes with embarrassment once a tipsy bishop departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is slang for a heavy drinker, a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Part of a flight coming from best airport

indicators.note: the letters emerge from within the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A segment of a plane journey departing from a top-rated airport.
explanation.walkthrough: With the airport in the surface, flight suggests air travel, but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of steps between floors, and each single step is one unit of it.

clue.text: African country bordering a West African country

indicators.note: to border something is to lie around its edges, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa
taken as written
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Describing one African state as sharing a border with another in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: West African reads as one phrase, but West gives a letter on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-eastern Africa, beside Lake Malawi.

clue.text: Impoverished person’s urge to enter pub

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A penniless man feels the temptation to go into a tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is someone so poor that they live by asking strangers for money or food.

clue.text: Coach needs player on the bench to turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a substitute waits on the bench

explanation.surface: A sports coach needs a reserve to show up for the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach looks like a team manager, but it is the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a long-distance passenger vehicle, the same kind of road vehicle as a bus.

clue.text: Checked item on which kings and queens stand?

definitions.text: Checked item on which kings and queens stand?

blocks.clueFragment: Checked item on which kings and queens stand?
blocks.note: surface reading: royalty standing on an inspected platform or a patterned carpet
setter's reading: the chess pieces, standing on a chequered playing surface of sixty-four squares

explanation.walkthrough: Checked here means patterned in squares, and the kings and queens are chess pieces rather than monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: The game of chess is played on a square board of alternating light and dark squares.
